newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-GILLESPIE SHATTERS SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GILLESPIE SHATTERS SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Australian fast bowler Jason Gillespie claimed his first five-wicket haul in only his fourth test as South Africa slumped to 151 for seven at tea on the first day of the second test on Friday.

Gillespie shared four wickets with fellow pace man Glenn McGrath in the morning session but then grabbed the first three wickets after lunch to finish the afternoon session with five for 37 from 17 hostile and accurate overs.
After lunching at 64 for four, South Africa soon lost Daryll Cullinan for 34 to a thick edge which was snapped up by Shane Warne in the gully with the total on 70.
Gillespie then removed Herschelle Gibbs' off stump with a classic off-cutter for 31 and had Shaun Pollock lbw next delivery -- the fourth duck of the innings.
At that point South Africa were 95 for seven but the veterans Brian McMillan and Dave Richardson offered desperately needed and belated resistance with an unbroken eighth wicket partnership of 56.
The 33-year-old McMillan, who missed the first test defeat in Johannesburg because of injury, was 34 not out at tea with 37-year-old Richardson on 25.

Earlier, Mark Taylor's decision to bowl first was immediately vindicated on a green, moist pitch when opener Gary Kirsten could only fend a Gillespie lifter into the hands of Matthew Hayden for a duck in the sixth over of the innings.
Jacques Kallis also failed to trouble the scorers. Another Gillespie lifter saw him lob a simple catch to Greg Blewett at backward short leg.
Opener Adam Bacher survived an impassioned appeal for a catch at the wicket before he had scored but then fell to McGrath for 11, caught in the gully by Matthew Elliott.

With wickets falling at 13, 17 and 21, a grim faced South African captain Hansie Cronje strode to the wicket but his determination amounted to nothing -- literally. He became the third duck when he was bowled off an inside edge by McGrath to leave his team on 22 for four.
